newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine mortgage bank sale aims at small holders.
newsitem.headline: Argentine mortgage bank sale aims at small holders.

text.p: The head of state mortgage lender Banco Hipotecario Nacional, approved for privatization by the Senate Wednesday night, said Thursday it would pass to the hands of small shareholders rather one major operator.

BHN Chairman Pablo Rojo told local radio that the sell-off passed by Congress, which now only needs presidential approval to become law, set down that nobody can own more than 5.0 percent of the bank's share capital.

"This is very different to the privatization of other state companies because we are not looking for a strategic operator. We want the bank to have broad ownership, spread among small and medium shareholders," said Rojo.

Peronist President Carlos Menem hopes the sale will raise about $3 billion to fund housing and infrastructure projects. The revenue will go into a Trustee Fund for Regional Infrastructure, with $100 million to be put aside for building homes and the rest being divided equally between the central government and provinces for infrastructure projects.
